definition: Sunspring is a 2016 experimental science fiction short film entirely written by an artificial intelligence bot using neural networks.
details: It was conceived by BAFTA-nominated filmmaker Oscar Sharp and NYU AI researcher Ross Goodwin and produced by film production company, End Cue along with Allison Friedman and Andrew Swett. It stars Thomas Middleditch, Elisabeth Grey, and Humphrey Ker as three people, namely H, H2, and C, living in a future world and eventually connecting with each other through a love triangle. The script of the film was authored by a recurrent neural network called long short-term memory (LSTM) by an AI bot named Benjamin. Originally made for the Sci-Fi-London film festival's 48hr Challenge, it was released online by technology news website Ars Technica on 9 June 2016.

explainer.lead: Sunspring is a 2016 experimental science fiction short film whose screenplay was written entirely by a neural network. It matters as an early, widely publicized demonstration that AI could produce a shootable narrative script.

tiers.eli5: A short sci-fi film where the script was generated by a computer program rather than a human writer, and actors performed what it produced.
tiers.practitioner: It is cited as a reference point for machine-generated creative text and for the workflow of handing model output to human directors and actors; the pitfall illustrated is output that is surreal and inconsistent, needing human framing to become usable.
tiers.paperLevel: The script was authored by a long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network trained on screenplays; the work is an artistic demonstration, not a quantitative study.

explainer.example: Actors Thomas Middleditch, Elisabeth Grey and Humphrey Ker play H, H2 and C in a future world linked by a love triangle, performing dialogue generated by the LSTM.
